Article Title: Oil prices slip over $1 as US weighs ‘D-Day’ Iran sanctions; Strait of Hormuz shipping risks in focus
Article Text:
Oil prices slip over $1 per barrel

US threatens wider economic pressure

Iran warns of oil export halt

Oil prices eased more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors booked profits ahead of a US announcement on new sanctions against Iran, with markets weighing the possibility of further disruption to Middle Eastern supplies.Brent crude declined 1.90% to $92.60 a barrel while WTI crude fell 1.96% to $85.35 per barrel, as of 7:30 am IST.The decline came after both benchmarks gained more than 5% last week, marking their second consecutive weekly rises. The gains followed a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks, which had contributed to a sharp reduction in oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway had previously carried a fifth of the world's oil supply.The latest focus is on Washington's planned sanctions. US treasury decretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to hold a press conference at 2 pm EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday and has warned of "the toughest sanctions in history" against Iran. US President Donald Trump has also threatened measures against countries trading with Tehran."But if the US measures do work as intended, Iran's ability to respond via increased violence becomes a growing risk for energy markets to consider."Iran has rejected the planned sanctions, while President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for a diplomatic resolution.The impact is already being felt in the country's oil trade. Trade sources cited by Reuters said that offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers had fallen and prices had risen after a US blockade reduced Tehran's shipments.At the same time, Iran allowed several Iraqi oil tankers to travel through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.Washington has described the coming measures as "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled", with Iran's trading partners among those expected to be targeted.Iran has responded by threatening to halt all oil exports from the Gulf if the economic pressure continues.Bessent is expected to outline the measures during Monday's press conference, as Washington steps up economic pressure on a country that has faced almost continuous sanctions since the 1979 Islamic Revolution."At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," Bessent wrote in an opinion piece published in the Financial Times on Sunday.He has also warned countries maintaining economic and financial ties with Iran about the consequences of continuing those relationships, without specifying the measures Washington plans to impose."They would do well to consider the consequences of sustaining it," he wrote in the Financial Times.China has also been urged by Bessent to cooperate with the US, particularly as half of its oil imports from the Gulf region come from the region. China's embassy in Washington said "sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem," while calling for diplomacy.Iran has spent days preparing for the new sanctions and has issued increasingly strong warnings over its possible response.Earlier on Sunday, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said that Tehran could respond economically if the pressure continued."If the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported, neither through the Strait of Hormuz nor from anywhere in the Persian Gulf," Rezaei wrote in a social media post."Iran will regard any country’s participation in or support for America’s economic war against the Iranian people as an act of war."Iran's ability to disrupt energy supplies remains a major concern for oil markets. The country has retained enough missile and drone capability to threaten Gulf neighbours and oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, while shipping through the waterway has been brought close to a standstill.The condition of Iran's nuclear programme remains unknown, while the US and Israel have sought to destroy it.Meanwhile, oil prices have remained volatile as the conflict continues to rage. However, the latest spike is far below the $126 a barrel level seen earlier in the conflict.
Article Summary: Brent crude down 1.90% to $92.60 a barrel, while WTI crude falls 1.96%. Both benchmarks gained more than 5% last week, marking their second consecutive weekly rises. The gains followed a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks, which contributed to a sharp reduction in oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: KPMG Australia to cut 5% of workforce amid scandal, weak growth outlook
Article Text:
KPMG Australia to cut 5% of workforce amid scandal, weak growth outlook

Revenue falls as consulting business takes hit

Government scrutiny intensifies

KPMG Australia is reducing its workforce by about 5% as the firm continues to deal with the fallout from a scandal involving confidential client information and faces a subdued economic outlook.The cuts will affect 27 partners and about 360 employees, with consulting and business services expected to account for most of the reduction.The move comes as the firm undergoes a leadership overhaul following allegations that staff used inside information to secure lucrative audit contracts. The allegations were made by whistleblowers in March and have since brought KPMG Australia under intense scrutiny from the Australian government and major corporate clients.John Sams, who became KPMG Australia's CEO last month, acknowledged the challenges that the firm is facing."We recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue ⁠to do to rebuild trust," Sams said in a statement cited by Reuters .KPMG Australia said it expected economic growth to remain subdued until at least 2028. It said this would weigh on client investment and result in longer decision-making timeframes."While these conditions are likely to persist, we remain focused ⁠on what we can control," Sams said.The firm's revenue fell 1% to $1.6 billion in the year ended June 2026. Consulting revenue dropped 17%, with the loss of government contracts contributing to the decline.However, four of KPMG Australia's five divisions recorded higher revenue during the year. Deal advisory and infrastructure revenue increased 3%, while tax and legal, and audit and assurance each recorded 11% growth. Revenue in the mid-market and private division rose 6.4%.Average pay for equity partners declined 13% during the year as KPMG dealt with the impact of the scandal and reviewed its costs.The controversy has also resulted in several senior departures, including the firm's former CEO, audit boss and chairman, as well as senior audit partners.KPMG Australia has agreed not to bid for new federal government work until September 30. The Australian government said in June that reviews into the firm's governance, culture, ethics and integrity were underway.The latest developments come as the government considers wider changes to the country's accounting sector. Last month, it said it was considering breaking up the Big Four: KPMG, Deloitte, EY and PwC.The firms currently operate as partnerships rather than companies and are therefore not subject to supervision by Australia's corporate regulator. That arrangement could change under reforms being considered by the government.The sector has faced a series of controversies in recent years. A tax leaks scandal at PwC in 2023 prompted parliamentary inquiries, although most of the recommendations have yet to be implemented.Alongside the workforce reduction, KPMG Australia said it planned to simplify parts of its structure, with the aim of creating more integrated teams and aligning them more closely with its global advisory services.
Article Summary: KPMG Australia to cut 5% of workforce amid scandal, weak growth outlook. Firm's revenue fell 1% to $1.6 billion in the year ended June 2026. Consulting revenue dropped 17%, with loss of government contracts contributing to decline.

Article Title: SIM card rules 2026: What changes from August 24 and how many connections can you have
Article Text:
Govt has directed the telecos to strictly enforce the rule of not issuing a new connection to any subscriber already having nine SIMs (representative image)

How the new SIM verification system will work

How many mobile connections can you have?

Most of India: Maximum 9 mobile connections

Jammu and Kashmir: Maximum 6

Assam: Maximum 6

North-East: Maximum 6

When will the new system become fully real-time?

The government has directed telecom service providers to stop individuals from obtaining mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit of nine, with a new system coming into effect from August 24.Under the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) instructions, telecom companies will have to identify subscribers who seek a new mobile connection after already reaching the maximum number allowed in their name and inform them that another connection cannot be provided.The move will initially operate on a post-facto basis, allowing telecom operators to carry out the verification one day after a connection is enrolled.However, the government has asked operators to shift to a real-time system for identifying and preventing excess connections by November 30.From August 24, telecom operators will have to take technical and organisational measures to identify subscribers attempting to obtain connections beyond the prescribed limit.The DoT circular said: “From 24.8.2026 onward, TSPs shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to identify each subscriber who seeks to obtain mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit using the representative image of the photo of a subscriber....andcommunicate to him that he already has maximum number of mobile connections permitted to an individual and accordingly, a new mobile connection cannot be provided to him. ”To help operators carry out these checks, the DoT will make available on the Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) from August 23 a representative image of the photograph of every subscriber who has already reached the prescribed limit.Telecom companies will have to download these images daily and use them to identify subscribers attempting to obtain additional mobile connections.Until the system is fully implemented on a post-facto basis, any connection activated beyond the permitted limit during a day will have to be immediately suspended until the issue is resolved.Under existing DoT instructions issued on August 9, 2012, an individual can hold a maximum of nine mobile connections in their name across all telecom operators and licensed service areas in India.However, a lower limit applies in certain regions:Customers are also required to provide a declaration in the Customer Application Form (CAF) stating the mobile connections already held in their name across telecom operators and licensed service areas.The government has set August 24 as the date from which telecom operators must begin identifying subscribers trying to obtain connections beyond the permitted limit.The initial system can operate on a post-facto basis, but telecom operators have been directed to integrate the checks into the enrolment and activation process in real time by November 30.The respective Licensed Service Areas (LSAs) will be the competent authorities to decide issues arising from implementation of the instructions.The DoT has directed telecom operators to decline new connections to subscribers who already have the maximum number of permitted SIM cards.
Article Summary: The government has directed telecom service providers to stop individuals from obtaining mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit of nine. The new system will come into effect from August 24. The initial system can operate on a post- facto basis, but telecom operators have been directed to integrate the checks into the enrolment and activation process in real time by November 30.

Article Title: Oil price today: Brent crude stays above $90 as Middle East standoff intensifies
Article Text:
Oil prices continue to soar

Oil prices remained steady on Tuesday after sliding more than 2% the previous day, with investors weighing the potential impact of tougher US sanctions on Iran against ongoing risks to oil supplies.Brent crude gained 0.09% to $92.25 a barrel while WTI crude was 0.35% up to $85.31 a barrel.The two benchmarks had fallen more than 2% on Monday. Supply concerns remained in focus after the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said that an oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile and disabled about 9 nautical miles (16.7 km) northeast of Oman's Ash Shishah on Tuesday.The incident came as tensions around the Strait of Hormuz continued. Iran maintains that it should control the key waterway, which before the war began in February typically carried cargoes equal to about 20% of global oil use.Iran on Monday also identified 45 tankers it said had violated its rules for crossing the strait and warned that it could take action against them, including confiscating their cargoes.At the same time, the US stepped up economic pressure on Iran. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent announced an expansion of sanctions designed to cut off Iran's economic lifeline and force an end to the war between the two countries.Bessent said countries would have to end their business ties with Iran or risk losing access to the dollar-based financial system. He did not, however, name the countries that would face the measures or say when they would come into effect, saying they would be given time to comply with the new directive.The US has also kept the possibility of military action open. Defense secretary Pete Hegseth said on Monday that the US would not rule out using military force against Iran. Analysts cited by Reuters said the shift towards economic coercion had reduced concerns over threats to Middle Eastern oil supplies arising from the war.The conflict has already put pressure on oil reserves, with countries drawing down their commercial and strategic stockpiles following supply disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28.US crude reserves held in the strategic petroleum reserve fell by about 3.7 million barrels last week to 289.7 million barrels, the department of energy reported on Monday. That was the lowest level since November 1982.Meanwhile, though oil prices have stayed volatile amid the ongoing Middle East chaos, the spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel levels seen earlier in the conflict.
Article Summary: Brent crude gained 0.09% to $92.25 a barrel while WTI crude was 0.35% up to $85.31 a barrel. The two benchmarks had fallen more than 2% on Monday. An oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile and disabled about 9 nautical miles (16.7 km) northeast of Oman's Ash Shishah.

Article Title: ‘Hire and train Americans’: JD Vance defends proposed six-figure H-1B fee
Article Text:
File photo: Vice President JD Vance (Picture credit: AP)

DHS proposes new H-1B fee

New proposal follows court setback over $100,000 fee

Indians among major H-1B beneficiaries

US Vice President JD Vance has backed the Trump administration’s proposal to impose a new $103,265 fee on most new H-1B visa petitions, saying American companies should prioritise hiring and training US workers.Vance shared a US media report on the proposal on X and wrote, “If an American corporation needs workers, it should hire and train Americans.”The proposed fee was announced by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in a filing on Monday. It would apply to all H-1B cap-subject petitions, including those eligible for the advanced degree exemption, and would be payable when the petition is filed.The proposed charge would be in addition to other applicable H-1B fees and payments.According to the DHS filing, the $103,265 fee would serve as a dedicated revenue mechanism to recover part of the government's costs of administering the lawful immigration system. The costs would cover activities across the Department of Homeland Security as well as the Departments of Justice, State and Labour.The public has 30 days to submit comments on the proposal. The rule is not final and could take months to become official, particularly if it faces legal challenges.Also read: US proposes $103,265 H-1B fee: Hiring set to become more costly H-1B visas allow foreign professionals to work in specialised occupations in the US. Applicants generally need a bachelor's degree or an equivalent qualification. The visa is valid for three years and can be renewed for another three years.The latest proposal follows a legal setback for the Trump administration over an earlier $100,000 H-1B fee.In June, US District Judge Leo Sorokin struck down the previous fee. According to CNN, the Boston-based judge found that the president lacked the authority to impose the requirement and held that Congress, rather than the president, had the power to change federal immigration policy to include such a requirement.Sorokin viewed the earlier payment as a tax.The earlier $100,000 payment had been introduced through a presidential proclamation in September 2025 and faced legal challenges.The new $103,265 proposal is based on a different legal authority and would establish a separate fee regime for cap-subject H-1B petitions.Under the proposal, the fee would apply to H-1B petitions subject to the annual cap. The proposed charge would not cover H-1B petitions that are exempt from the annual cap.The US has an annual quota of 85,000 new H-1B visas, including 20,000 reserved for applicants with advanced degrees.The proposed fee would therefore substantially increase the cost for employers sponsoring workers through the cap-subject H-1B programme.The proposed fee could also affect Indian professionals, who account for a large share of H-1B visa recipients.2.83 lakh H-1B visas were allotted to Indians in fiscal 2025, accounting for 70% of the total visas, including extensions.For new visas for initial employment, Indians received nearly 58,000 visas, roughly half of the total new visas, including cap-exempt visas.The proposed $103,265 fee would be separate from the earlier $100,000 payment introduced in September 2025.The earlier measure applied to hiring H-1B workers from outside the US and its implementation was vacated by a district court in June, with the government's appeal pending.The proposed new fee, meanwhile, is tied to whether an H-1B petition is cap-subject, rather than simply whether the worker is inside or outside the US.
Article Summary: US Vice President JD Vance has backed the Trump administration’s proposal to impose a new $103,265 fee on most new H-1B visa petitions. Vance said American companies should prioritise hiring and training US workers. The proposed fee was announced by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in a filing on Monday.

Article Title: Honey to hockey sticks: Trump's 50% tariff net catches 550+ Canadian goods
Article Text:
Trump's 50% tariff net catches 550+ Canadian goods

What is caught in the tariff net?

Why has Trump imposed the 50% levy?

Canada prepares to retaliate

Honey, makeup, Christmas decorations and a host of other everyday products have fallen victim to the latest US-Canada trade crossfire.More than 550 Canadian goods are now facing a steep 50% US tariff that came into force on Saturday. The list also includes kitchenware, smartphones, golf equipment, cosmetics, sports gear and household items.The new duties are expected to cover around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, equivalent to about 5% of the $381.92 billion of products Canada exported to the US last year.The tariff does not cover most of Canada’s exports, but the 50% rate could still weigh on consumers if it remains in place. Importers, the businesses bringing goods into the US, pay the tariffs, with at least some of that additional cost typically passed on to shoppers. The latest duties come on top of price increases linked to tariffs imposed earlier.The breadth of the new list means the impact could show up across a wide range of shopping categories, as well as in expenses such as home-building.And the tariff fight is already set for another round. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has promised “dollar for dollar” retaliation from September 8, while US President Donald Trump has threatened further tariffs on Canadian products, including automobiles.The Trump administration had said last month that its planned 50% tariffs would cover products such as hockey sticks, wine and cement. The final list runs much wider, covering more than 550 goods.Among the products facing the new tariff are natural honey, bulbs for plants such as tulips and lilies, some fresh cut flowers, seeds for beets, onions and other vegetables, horsehair, tortoise shells, antlers and various animal products.The list also includes beer, vermouth and cider, along with furniture knobs, wallpaper, lighting fixtures, plates, cups, bowls and other kitchen or tableware.Paints, varnishes, vinyl tile floor coverings and various plywood sheets have also been targeted, as have ice skates, golf equipment, fishing rods and other sports accessories.Consumers could also see the impact on perfumes, makeup and manicure preparations, as well as suitcases, bags, gloves and coats.Toys and certain “articles for Christmas festivities” are on the list, alongside digital cameras and recording equipment, smartphones, video game consoles, envelopes, cigarette paper and toilet or facial tissue.The tariffs were imposed under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, a Great Depression-era provision that had never previously been used. It allows the president to impose import taxes of up to 50% on goods from countries accused of discriminating against US businesses.Trump has said Canada discriminated against US automobiles, alcohol and dairy products, particularly after the introduction of his earlier import taxes last year.However, the products covered by the latest tariffs extend far beyond those categories.Cars, auto parts and energy products were excluded from the latest tariffs, but they remained central to negotiations between the two countries, which collapsed at the eleventh hour over the weekend.Carney said on Monday that Washington’s proposals for the auto sector would “gradually dismantle” Canadian production.He also pointed to Canada’s position as the largest customer for US automobiles and questioned what the latest US move would mean for workers in states such as Ohio, Kentucky and Alabama whose jobs depend on that demand.Carney said Canada would respond to the new US tariffs with measures of its own.On Saturday, he announced that Canada would begin dollar-for-dollar countermeasures on September 8. The measures will target US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.Carney said further details would be announced later.The possibility of the trade dispute spreading to more products and sectors grew on Monday.Ontario Premier Doug Ford told AP in an exclusive interview that “everything is on the table”. He said the province would be ready to cut off electricity and critical minerals to the US if the trade war worsened.“Trump "underestimates Canada. We’re all in,” Ford said. He also urged Canada to consider using oil and potash, both major exports, as leverage.Trump, meanwhile, said his administration would increase tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel to 50% from January 1, 2027.Canada currently faces a broader 25% tariff on autos, while most steel imports already face a 50% sectoral tariff.Trump accused Canada of “ripping off” the US for years through what he called “ridiculously high tariffs” on American farmers. “WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!” he added in a Monday Truth Social post.
Article Summary: More than 550 Canadian goods are now facing a steep 50% US tariff. The list also includes kitchenware, smartphones, golf equipment, cosmetics, sports gear and household items. The new duties are expected to cover around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, equivalent to about 5% of the $381.92 billion of products Canada exported to the US last year.

Article Title: Meiji Seika to push new vaccine with SII in India
Article Text:
Meiji Seika, SII tie up to bring Japanese Encephalitis vaccine to India; Medreich eyes expansion

TOKYO: Meiji Seika Pharma-owned Medreich Pharma is eyeing inorganic growth and more generics supply from India, while the parent has tied up with Serum Institute of India (SII) to launch Japanese Encephalitis vaccine in the country."SII will take the required approval to provide the vaccine for children in India. Our subsidiary has already marketed this vaccine in Japanese market. Hopefully, next year SII will apply and try to take the approval in India and then they will market this vaccine," Meiji Seika Pharma COO for pharma segment Toshiaki Nagasato said after a meeting with commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal here on Monday. The Japanese company is seeking that the approval should be accelerated."SII manufactures at the lowest cost. We believe SII will launch the vaccine at affordable and lowest cost. SII technology offcials also came to Japan to understand the technology in Japan," Nagasato said.According to WHO, there are three types of Japanese Encephalitis vaccines, which are given to children. Japan has the technology to help combat the disease that it once grappled with and combined with India's low cost manufacturing capability the partnership could help children.SII and Meiji Seika Pharma had announced the achievement of the first milestone last April.Nagasato said the Japanese company is looking to invest into its Indian subsidiary Medreich, which it had acquired in 2014, although he refused to disclose the amount. He said the idea is to help expand the Indian company's generic operations within the country and also for exports to countries, such as UK, Canada and other European and African companies.
Article Summary: Meiji Seika Pharma-owned Medreich Pharma is eyeing inorganic growth and more generics supply from India. The parent has tied up with Serum Institute of India (SII) to launch Japanese Encephalitis vaccine in the country.

Article Title: Mumbai only Indian city in global Work From Anywhere Index; ranks ahead of London, Miami
Article Text:
Mumbai only Indian city in global Work From Anywhere Index

Why is Mumbai on the list?

How work is changing travel plans

Mumbai, long known for its Bollywood glitz, Marine drive charm and dream-city vibe, is now emerging as a destination for professionals looking to work from anywhere. The city has become the only Indian entry in IWG's 2026 Work From Anywhere Index, scoring 77 and ranking ahead of global cities including London and Miami.Mumbai's debut in the fourth edition of the annual index puts it among destinations assessed not just for their appeal to travellers, but also for how well they can double up as temporary offices. IWG's index evaluates cities on factors including climate, broadband speed, accommodation, transport, food, culture and the availability of flexible workspaces.Mumbai scored well on transport costs, co-working and flexible workspace availability, climate and accommodation. However, its scores were relatively lower for broadband speed and quality, availability of local events and the happiness index.The city's inclusion also comes against the backdrop of India's expanding flexible workspace market. According to data from Cushman & Wakefield's Global Trends in Flexible Office 2025 report, India scored 100 on the flexible workspace maturity index, ahead of the UK at 98, France at 97 and the US at 81.India was also the largest flexible office market in the Asia-Pacific region, with 79.7 million square feet of stock across its top eight cities as of the second quarter of 2025. The stock is expected to cross 100 million square feet in 2026, according to the release.Mumbai's place on the index comes as Work From Anywhere policies increasingly blur the line between working and travelling. Separate research commissioned by IWG found that 51 per cent of workers surveyed said their employer already offered a Work From Anywhere policy."90% say WFA has improved their work-life balance, and 80% say it has improved productivity," the release said. It added that 62 per cent of respondents would consider changing jobs for a better Work From Anywhere policy.The flexibility is also influencing holiday plans. Nearly half of the respondents, or 48 per cent, said they planned to extend a holiday or mini-break by working remotely in 2026. Another 46 per cent said they were more likely to do so than last year, while 43 per cent said they had already worked remotely from a holiday destination without using annual leave.However, the workplace survey covered 2,000 hybrid office workers in the UK and the US between July 6 and July 9, 2026. Its findings therefore do not specifically represent Indian workers.Bangkok topped the global list with a score of 106.5, followed by Tokyo at 96.5 and Barcelona at 95.5. Porto and Vancouver completed the top five.Budapest, Naples, Medellin, Lisbon and Seoul rounded out the top 10 Work From Anywhere destinations for 2026.
Article Summary: Mumbai is the only Indian entry in IWG's 2026 Work From Anywhere Index. The city scored 77, ranking ahead of global cities including London and Miami. It scored well on transport costs, co-working and flexible workspace availability, climate and accommodation.

Article Title: Resona Bank deepens ties with Tata Cap
Article Text:
RBI

MUMBAI: Japan's Resona Bank on Monday announced a tie-up with Tata Capital to provide its clients better access to financing solutions and opportunities in India using the non-bank lender's local network. The announcement follows a $20 million investment by Resona Bank as a limited partner in Tata Capital Growth Fund III LP, which invests in Tata Capital Growth Fund III, a fund managed by Tata Capital, as per an official statement. However, the Japanese lender did not reveal the timeline of this investment. Under a memorandum of understanding (MoU) announced on Monday, both Tata Capital and Resona Bank will leverage their respective strengths in the Indian market, it said, adding that this is a non-exclusive collaboration under which opportunities will be explored through Tata Capital's network.
Article Summary: Japan's Resona Bank announces a tie-up with Tata Capital. Announcement follows a $20 million investment by Resona in Tata Capital Growth Fund III LP. Both banks will leverage their respective strengths in the Indian market, it said.

Article Title: Government eyes 3000 crore by selling 6% in Hindustan Copper
Article Text:
Govt to sell up to 6% stake in Hindustan Copper via OFS to raise around Rs 3,000 crore

MUMBAI: Govt is selling up to 6% in Hindustan Copper at a floor price of Rs 514 per share through an offer for sale (OFS) to mobilise about Rs 3,000 crore. The floor price for the OFS is at an 11.6% discount to the stock's closing price of Rs 573.6 on BSE on Monday. This is the 10th divestment offer in the current fiscal.According to the company's disclosures on BSE, govt is offering to sell a little over 2.9 crore shares (3% of the company's equity capital) through the OFS, which will open today. Depending on the demand, govt may offer another 2.9 crore shares to investors, it said.Retail investors will be able to bid on the second day of the offer, that is, Aug 26. "10% of the offer is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares reserved for eligible employees," secretary, DIPAM, govt's divestment department, said through a post on X (formerly Twitter).Currently, govt holds 66.1% in the copper miner and producer, shareholding data on BSE showed. Post the successful divestment in the company, govt's stake would come down to a little over 60%. DAM Capital Advisors, Emkay Global Financial Services and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities are managing the offer for govt, the OFS notice on BSE showed. This divestment comes within three weeks of the most successful OFS in India.On Aug 6, govt closed the offer to sell 10% in life insurance major LIC and mobilised Rs 31,515 crore from the market. It was the biggest such offer in India ever.Till date in FY27, govt has mobilised Rs 52,716 crore from nine divestments and some receipts from SUUTI. The Budget had set a Rs 80,000-crore divestment target for the current year.
Article Summary: Govt to sell up to 6% stake in Hindustan Copper via OFS to raise around Rs 3,000 crore. The floor price for the OFS is at an 11.6% discount to the stock's closing price of Rs 573.6 on BSE. This is the 10th divestment offer in the current fiscal.

Article Title: Government looks to add more AI partners for digital projects
Article Text:
Govt reopens AI/ML vendor empanelment, looks to expand tech partner pool for Digital India projects

NEW DELHI: Govt is looking at widening its pool of technology partners for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) projects, with the ministry of electronics and IT reopening empanelment of agencies that can deploy AI/ML resources across govt programmes.The fresh tender has been issued by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), which functions under MeitY, and seeks to bring more companies onto an existing panel created for AI/ML manpower augmentation and AI-driven project delivery under the Digital India programme.The move follows the first round of empanelment, in which six companies - Tata Consultancy Services, NEC India, Kyndryl, CoRover, Innefu Labs and Cactus Technology Solutions - were selected to work on govt AI projects. Companies joining through the latest round will have to accept the rate card discovered during the earlier empanelment process, indicating that the exercise is aimed at expanding the vendor base rather than undertaking a fresh price discovery.NeGD published the reopened Request for Empanelment on Aug 10, with bid submissions scheduled to close on Sept 7. The bids are expected to be opened on Sept 8.The empanelled companies can be tapped for deployment of AI and machine learning professionals and execution of AI-led projects across government departments and Digital India initiatives.
Article Summary: Govt reopens AI/ML vendor empanelment, looks to expand tech partner pool for Digital India projects. The fresh tender has been issued by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), which functions under MeitY.

Article Title: Labour survey 2026 likely to track digital, platform workers
Article Text:
India’s PLFS 2026 to count gig, platform workers separately for first time

NEW DELHI: In a first, India's official statistical machinery is likely to provide data on the digital and platform-based workers in the upcoming annual periodic labour force survey (PLFS), a move which will help policymakers assess the true scope and nature of the fast-growing gig workforce in India, an official told TOI."In PLFS 2026, data on digital platform workers - a subset of gig workers is being collected among the workers classified in the existing PLFS framework as self-employed, regular wage/salaried or casual workers on an experimental basis. All such workers will be included in the broader self- employed category," the official said. The survey results are expected in March 2027 and will provide the maiden official estimate of the number of people working as food delivery executives, drivers and as a myriad of home service providers, among other things in the country.Currently, anyone who engages in market activities for profit is covered under the PLFS framework as a worker, though it does not capture data on people engaged in the gig or digital and platform-based work separately, thus making it difficult to identify gig and platform workers among the total workforce. Drawing upon a 2022 NITI Aayog study, a labour ministry think tank VV Giri National Labour Institute in its latest study expects the gig and platform workforce in the country to grow over 6 crores by 2047 - constituting nearly 15% of the total non-agricultural workforce in the country."Along with enumeration, other key characteristics of such workers, which will include their earnings, working hours, working conditions will also be captured in the upcoming labour force survey. This will help govt to formulate welfare policies for them and implement the provisions of the social security code," the official added.
Article Summary: In a first, India's official statistical machinery is likely to provide data on the digital and platform-based workers in the upcoming annual periodic labour force survey (PLFS) The survey results are expected in March 2027 and will provide the maiden official estimate of the number of people working as food delivery executives, drivers and as a myriad of home service providers.

Article Title: India a safe base, Piyush Goyal tells Japanese investors
Article Text:
Piyush Goyal pitches India as trusted, tariff-friendly base for Japanese firms

TOKYO: It isn't just high growth and an expanding market that make India an attractive destination for investors. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Monday added India's long list of FTAs and the possibility of Japanese companies using the preferential tariffs to set up a base to it and looking at it as a gateway to the world.And, he topped it up by positioning India as a safe base for Japanese companies as data is protected, intellectual property is secure and where an entrepreneur does not "go missing only to be found as a professor in some other country". The last three were seen as a dig at China, amid indications that companies, including Google, are looking to shift a part of their mobile manufacturing facility in what has come to be known as "China+1" strategy."India is not a plus one country. India stands on its own merits as a trusted partner. We don't steal anybody's technology, we don't copy anyone's intellectual property products and bring it into the market. In India you have a growing middle class, the fastest growing major economy in the globe and most importantly the youthful talent," Goyal said. He also signalled that govt was willing to relax rules, provided it does not result in imports from "one country", which is not conducive for fair trading practices and often supplies goods at predatory pricing.While Japan has been pushing for deeper ties with countries such as India, the recent trade tussle with China has added to the urgency.The minister also made a strong case for India as a good fit to address issues that Japan was facing. "One can clearly see that for an economy like Japan, which has very good technologies but not enough people, which has excellent business practices but not enough market, India can be an excellent partner, which provides economies of scale with a large domestic market and India which has opened its doors to international engagement with several FTAs. .. we are a trusted partner in global supply chains and for Japan to enjoy competitive advantage over other countries, working with India, will give it a natural edge."As he courted multiple investors, he asserted that govt was willing to address individual concerns that Japanese companies may have and cited two cases on Monday itself when he spoke to officials in India to find a solution to the issues flagged by a semiconductor equipment manufacturer and another by an auto components player.During another meeting, Goyal urged Japanese steel makers to buy India-made steel for local requirements instead of importing it into the country.He also said that India is negotiating trade deals with at least eight-nine trading partners that together account for another $15 trillion of GDP. The country's FTAs would eventually cover about 75% of global trade.
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal pitches India as trusted, tariff- friendly base for Japanese firms. Goyal: "For Japan to enjoy competitive advantage over other countries, working with India, will give it a natural edge" India is negotiating trade deals with at least eight-nine trading partners that together account for another $15 trillion of GDP.

Article Title: TCS to acquire Porsche arm for $373 million, inks $1.4 billion deal
Article Text:
TCS to acquire Porsche tech subsidiary MHP for $373 million in mega AI deal

TCS, Porsche seal $1.4-billion five-year partnership for AI-led automotive transformation

BENGALURU: In a mega deal that boosts its manufacturing and AI playbook, TCS will acquire MHP Management, the consulting and technology subsidiary of German sports car maker Porsche, for $373 million. The transaction will also anchor a five-year strategic partnership worth $1.4 billion.The partnership will focus on driving AI-led transformation across Porsche's engineering, manufacturing, operations, customer experience and enterprise functions, while also developing next-generation automotive technology services and software-defined mobility platforms.Porsche said the decision is part of its "Sportwagenschmiede 35" strategy, which aims to strengthen profitability and cash flow through 2035. The sports car manufacturer said it plans to sharpen its strategic focus by concentrating on its core business.TCS said its Netherlands subsidiary, Tata Consultancy Services Netherlands, approved the acquisition of MHP's equity shares from Porsche and signed a share purchase agreement for the proposed transaction. The acquisition is subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions and is expected to be completed within three to four months.The partnership with Porsche will serve as an anchor for TCS's AI transformation strategy and position the leading Indian IT services company as a strategic consulting and technology partner for Porsche, while creating opportunities to expand its offerings among other automotive and industrial customers in Europe.MHP is a leading automotive and industrial consulting firm in Europe, with capabilities spanning business consulting, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, SAP transformation, manufacturing digitalisation, connected mobility and software-defined mobility. However, MHP will retain its brand and continue to operate as an independent consultancy under its existing name.TCS CEO K Krithivasan said, "As AI, software, and data redefine the automotive industry, this partnership brings together TCS' capabilities in AI, engineering, technology and business transformation with MHP's strong automotive consulting expertise. Together, we will industrialise AI at scale for Porsche, accelerating innovation across the value chain to deliver intelligent, software-defined mobility experiences of the future. "Dr Michael Leiters, CEO of Porsche, said, "Porsche is taking another important step in its strategy to focus resolutely on its core business with the transfer of MHP to Tata Consultancy Services. At the same time, we are gaining a strategic partner in TCS. By combining Porsche's automotive expertise with TCS' digital technology and AI capabilities, we will further strengthen our innovative power, increase efficiency, and boost our competitiveness in an increasingly data and software-driven world of mobility. "
Article Summary: TCS will acquire MHP Management, the consulting and technology subsidiary of German sports car maker Porsche. The transaction will also anchor a five-year strategic partnership worth $1.4 billion. MHP will retain its brand and continue to operate as an independent consultancy under its existing name.

Article Title: UPI@10: How platform changed the way we pay
Article Text:
UPI completes 10 years, growing from 1.8 crore transactions in FY17 to 24,162 crore in FY26

MUMBAI: Nearly one in two real-time payments in the world happen on the UPI platform. From 1.8 crore transactions in FY17, the year it was launched, to 24,162 crore transactions in FY26, UPI transactions have grown 13,000 times.Today, the payment platform completes 10 years since it went live for general public use after its initial launch by then RBI governor Raghuram Rajan through a pilot test in April 2016. How did the most successful innovation under NDA govt come about?According to AP Hota, founding chief of National Payments Corporation of India, during whose term most of NPCI's products, including UPI, were launched, the idea originated from a dilemma over how to increase the use of IMPS (Immediate Payment Service). IMPS was a real-time payment platform built by repurposing the national financial switch infrastructure created for ATM transactions which required real-time debits from bank accounts. Before IMPS, electronic payments largely mimicked traditional payments, with transactions taking place in batches.Initial brainstorming showed that merchants needed to receive money immediately, which cards could not provide.While IMPS enabled person-to-person transfers, it was not designed for customers who wanted to pull money."UPI began as an attempt to redesign IMPS so as to simplify merchant payments, involve non-bank payment providers, reduce e-commerce payment failures, and adopt open-source technology and APIs. These objectives led us to move away from IMPS and build an entirely new solution, retaining only its proven real-time settlement engine," said Hota."Pramod Verma (technology architect who helped design UPI's API-driven architecture and played a key role in shaping its open, interoperable framework) became involved, while Nandan Nilekani was already with us as our technology and public policy adviser. Pramod and Nandan came up with the idea of making the entire system API-driven, with third-party application service providers," said Hota, who worked with banks and fintech companies to expand the network.Dilip Asbe, current chief of NPCI, who was COO at the time of the launch and led much of the implementation, explained the design in a podcast with Verma in Aug last year. UPI's scale, they said, came from designing it not as a centralised application with a massive database but as a decentralised, open protocol that resolves payment addresses in real time across participating banks.The architects built advanced capabilities into the core protocol while adopting a phased rollout, starting with basic peer-to-peer transfers before introducing features such as recurring mandates.While UPI's scale is now measured in billions of transactions, Hota had forecast in his 2017 farewell speech that the platform would achieve a billion transactions a day within a few years.
Article Summary: UPI completes 10 years, growing from 1.8 crore transactions in FY17 to 24,162 crore in FY26. Nearly one in two real-time payments in the world happen on the UPI platform. UPI's scale came from designing it not as a centralised application with a massive database.

Article Title: Russian President Putin says will continue fertiliser supplies to India
Article Text:
Ahead of Putin’s India visit, Jaishankar delivers PM Modi’s message as Russia assures continued fertiliser supplies

NEW DELHI: Ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to India next month, external affairs minister S Jaishankar called on the President and handed over a personal message from PM Narendra Modi to him. Putin committed to continuing fertiliser supplies to India in the meeting.The minister said he briefed him about the "very productive" meeting of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation and also discussed important regional and global issues with the President.Modi and Putin will meet on the margins of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan on Aug 31-Sept 1 before Putin travels to India for the BRICS summit on September 12.In his remarks, Putin focused on growing trade and energy ties and also the issue of fertilisers, saying Russia is doing everything to resolve this issue for Indian farmers and for the country's agricultural sector."There are many items on the agenda, which extends far beyond energy supplies. Fertiliser shipments are among these matters. Russia is expanding its exports and are ready to continue doing so. There are other matters too regarding nuclear energy, cooperation in high technology and other sectors - they are all on the agenda, and there has been steady progress on all these fronts," said Putin, adding that after the slight decline last year, trade was again increasing."PM [Narendra Modi] deserves much of the credit for this, considering his commitment to keeping a close eye on the development of Russia-India relations," he said, adding he was looking forward to meeting him at the SCO summit and that the leaders may meet again this year. Jaishankar told Putin that Modi was looking forward to welcoming him for the BRICS summit.Jaishankar met Russian first deputy PM Denis Manturov earlier in the day. "Our discussions focused on our wide - ranging cooperation in trade, investments, energy, fertilisers, nuclear, connectivity, technology, space and mobility domains," he said.According to Jaishankar, both sides focused also on de-risking and diversifying and further expanding engagement with businesses by aligning institutional mechanisms with industry priorities, identifying practical bottlenecks and improving policy responsiveness.
Article Summary: Putin committed to continuing fertiliser supplies to India in the meeting. Putin focused on growing trade and energy ties and also the issue of fertilisers. Jaishankar told Putin that Modi was looking forward to welcoming him for the BRICS summit.

Article Title: As onion prices rise, Centre readies retail intervention in Delhi-NCR
Article Text:
Centre to sell subsidised onions at Rs 35/kg in Delhi-NCR as retail prices climb

NEW DELHI: The Centre is likely to begin selling onions at a subsidised price of Rs 35 per kg across Delhi-NCR later this week to rein in soaring retail prices. Officials said locations for the retail sale through mobile vans will be finalised over the next couple of days.Building on the success of similar interventions in previous years, the Centre on Monday started operation of ‘Kanda Express’ trains to transport onions from Nashik in Maharashtra to key consumption centres -- Delhi, Chennai, Kochi, Madurai and Guwahati.“The first priority is to offload bulk onions at major mandis to cool wholesale prices, which should eventually ease retail prices across Delhi-NCR,” a consumer affairs department official said.Govt is also planning retail market interventions at multiple locations in Delhi-NCR through mobile vans to ensure onions are available to consumers at the subsidised rate, the official added. Earlier such interventions in the region have been successful. Onion was selling at Rs 55 a kg in Delhi compared to Rs 35 a kilo a year back.Officials said that if required this initiative will be extended to other cities where retail price is higher than the average national price.“Onion availability is currently comfortable to meet domestic demand in the coming months supported by an estimated production of 307 lakh tonne in 2025-26 which is in line with the previous year’s production of 308 lakh tonne. In addition, buffer stocks are available for calibrated market intervention,” consumer affairs department said in an official statement. Onion prices have historically increased from Aug-Sept onwards owing to increased festive season, weather conditions, supply-chain movements and demand conditions during this period.
Article Summary: The Centre is likely to begin selling onions at a subsidised price of Rs 35 per kg. Locations for the retail sale through mobile vans will be finalised over the next couple of days. Onion was selling at Rs 55 a kg in Delhi compared to Rs 35 a kilo a year back.

Article Title: Stocking, speculation behind ‘unnatural’ sugar price surge: ISMA
Article Text:
Sugar prices jump 29% in a month, industry blames ‘speculative behaviour’ for artificial tightness

NEW DELHI: Sugar industry’s apex body ISMA on Monday said that there is no shortage of the sweetener while admitting that the spike in prices is “not natural” and is being fuelled by stocking by bulk consumers and “speculative behaviour”. The industry body said they want “rationalisation” of retail prices and are hopeful of a reduction in the coming days following multiple steps that govt has taken.The industry also dismissed allegations of diversion of sugar for ethanol production as a reason for tight supply of the sweetener and increasing prices. It said only 290 crore litres out of a total 1,200 crore litre of ethanol came from sugar during this ethanol supply year (Oct 2025- Sept 2026). “Only after ensuring availability for domestic consumers and adequate opening stock, allocation for diversion of sugar for ethanol is decided,” ISMA functionaries said.On Monday, the average all-India retail prices of sugar stood at Rs 63 per kg, 29% higher than Rs 48.7 per kilo a month back.Speaking to reporters, ISMA president Niraj Shirgaokar said that the increase is not being driven by any “actual shotfall” in availability.“The largest contributor has been speculative behaviour. A section of traders created a misleading impression of tightness, and in response, large bulk buyers who would normally procure just-in-time began stocking 1.5-2 months of supply in advance. That behaviour pulled sugar out of circulation and into godowns, creating artificial tightness that had nothing to do with actual availability,” he said.ISMA said that prices have risen also due to factors including lower production than estimated, weather conditions and pests that impacted the crop. The association functionaries said that millers got a good ex-mill price, which peaked Rs 58-59 a kg, due to this artificial rise in sugar prices and now it’s declining, which will soon be reflected in the retail market.Shirgaokar projected the closing stock of roughly 35 lakh tonne at the end of Sept calling it “a healthy buffer against normal domestic demand” He added govt’s duty-free import window, tightened stockholding limits, ongoing special crushing, and an early start to the new season would help in augmenting domestic supply and control prices.Asked about govt putting blame on industry for jacking up ex-mill prices, ISMA president said that the industry was not involved in creating any artificial scarcity and increasing rates. However, he did not rule out that some mills might be holding stocks and said the govt is looking into that.
Article Summary: Sugar industry’s apex body ISMA on Monday said that there is no shortage of the sweetener. ISMA president Niraj Shirgaokar said that the increase is not being driven by any ‘actual shotfall’ in availability.

Article Title: Trump’s ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ against Iran: What sanctions threat could mean for India
Article Text:
Indian exports to Iran declined from $3.5 billion in FY2019 to $1.2 billion in FY2026.

Operation Economic Outcast: What Bessent announced

What US steps could mean for India’s oil imports

What it could mean for India-Iran trade

Launching an ‘economic onslaught’ on Iran, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that President Donald Trump is making phone calls to world leaders with specific requests to stop all interactions with Iran.The move comes amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict which has shaken the world economy and global oil markets since the end of February this year. Bessent said Monday that the new US sanctions are intended to shut off every potential source of revenue for Iran, while warning other countries that continuing their economic ties with Tehran could expose them to retaliation.He said it was “no longer acceptable to operate in the gray spaces” of the conflict.The US has imposed sanctions on Iran for decades. These measures prevent designated entities from accessing the dollar-based financial system.Iran, however, has managed to evade the restrictions by quickly setting up new front companies and other entities, as well as registering vessels under new arrangements.“Iran now faces a very clear choice, with only two paths before them: complete global isolation and a subsistence economy, or a path back to normalcy with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy.Today, we are launching Operation Economic Outcast to foreclose every other option available to the Iranian regime,” Bessent said.“Beginning today, the actions of the Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the IRGC and the evil Iranian regime. We are enforcing a zero leakage approach. There will be no minimal breathing space for the regime to rebuild its capacity to inflict terror against America and the world,” he added.“Iran's enablers purchase, transport its petroleum. They facilitate the flow of its finances through exchange houses and free trade zones. They welcome Iran's flights and maintain registries on its behalf. They turn a blind eye to seaborne fuel transfers and overland transits. They condone illicit use of their banks, all the while concealing the extent of their complicity,” Bessent said, warning countries of secondary sanctions.He did not specify which countries could potentially be targeted with secondary US sanctions. China, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates, however, are Iran’s biggest trading partners.“Let there be no ambiguity as to the position of the United States,” Bessent told a news conference. “An economic engagement of any kind with this murderous regime will expose those responsible to the full reach of American power.”China buys crude oil in huge quantities from Iran. Asked specifically about possible sanctions on China, Bessent said, “We want to make clear today that no one is above the reach of US sanctions. We find that the best way to engage with countries is through quiet diplomacy.”The Treasury Department has also sanctioned nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels.China has been the largest purchaser of Iranian oil for several years, and the US has stepped up efforts to restrict those purchases. However, it has so far refrained from designating major Chinese banks that could be facilitating the oil trade.India has not been importing oil from Iran due to US sanctions. However, amidst the Middle East conflict when the Trump administration waived sanctions on Iran oil at sea to ease global crude oil prices, India also picked up Iranian crude to ease pressure on its energy security.In the last few months no fresh crude shipments from Iran have been picked, and India’s diversified oil procurement basket has meant that there are no disruptions in the absence of oil from Iran.Therefore, Iran oil being sanctioned would not impact India as much in terms of supply, as it would in terms of prices.China is the biggest importer of Iranian crude. But if the Trump administration’s pressure manages to reduce China’s imports, it will look elsewhere for its supplies. This in turn will likely raise global crude oil prices which would impact India.“India’s bigger risks are higher oil prices, disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, passed by the US Senate on August 7 by an 86–11 vote. If enacted, it could authorize tariffs of up to 100% against major buyers of Russian energy,” Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) founder Ajay Srivastava cautions.As of now it is unclear whether there would be any direct impact of the secondary sanctions that the US has threatened. The five broad fields of sanctions are: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping.Indian exports to Iran declined from $3.5 billion in FY2019 to $1.2 billion in FY2026. Rice made up $810 million of exports, followed by tea and coffee at $82 million, medicines at $63 million, bananas at $54 million, sugar at $48 million and pulses at $34 million.India’s imports from Iran have also dropped sharply, from $13.5 billion in FY2019, including $12.4 billion worth of crude oil, to below $375 million in FY2026.Bitumen was the largest import at $138 million, followed by apples at $41 million, almonds at $36 million and dates at $35 million.Meanwhile, according to a Reuters report, Indian exporters have said that planned new US sanctions on Iran, along with the UAE’s decision to suspend trade with Tehran, could disrupt India’s exports of rice, tea and pharmaceuticals to Iran. Much of this trade has been routed through Dubai’s port in recent years.India has remained one of Iran’s five largest trading partners, although bilateral trade has dropped by more than 90% from its FY2019 peak of $17 billion. Exports are now largely restricted to goods that are exempt from sanctions on humanitarian grounds.Exporters in India are concerned that the Trump administration’s plan could put further pressure on trade that has already been weakened by sanctions, cautious banks and shipping constraints.The United Arab Emirates last week suspended all trade activities, exchanges and financial transactions with Iran until further notice."We are already seeing indications that transactions and payment mechanisms traditionally routed through the UAE are exploring alternative jurisdictions," said Dev Garg, vice president of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation, suggesting Turkey as an alternative.In the first six months of 2026, India exported $383.11 million worth of rice to Iran, making the country the second-largest overseas market for premium rice, including long-grained basmati."Any prolonged disruption in this corridor will have a much greater bearing on the basmati industry, especially on millers and exporters in northern India than on India's overall non-basmati rice trade," Garg said.Until recently, Indian exporters generally received payments through an Indian authorised-dealer bank from the account of a UAE-based trader. Payments were made in dirhams, dollars or another permitted currency, while the trader separately received payment from its Iranian customer through banking channels that complied with legal requirements.India’s tea exports to Iran stood at $14.34 million during the first half of 2026. Prabhat Bezboruah, a senior tea planter and former chairman of the state-run Tea Board, said tea sales to Iran would be hit because a significant portion of the trade passes through the UAE.
Article Summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that President Donald Trump is making phone calls to world leaders with specific requests to stop all interactions with Iran. The move comes amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict which has shaken the world economy and global oil markets since the end of February.

Article Title: School holiday August 24: Are schools closed today due to heavy rain? Check state-wise updates
Article Text:
School holiday today, August 24: Odisha announces district closures amid heavy rain; check latest updates

Odisha schools closed in affected districts

Rain forecast across other states

How to check your school's status

Schools in several parts of India are facing heavy rainfall as the southwest monsoon remains active across the country on Monday, August 24, 2026. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rain in several states, with isolated areas of Odisha likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall.There is no nationwide school holiday for August 24. However, school closures are being decided locally according to rainfall, flooding, waterlogging, landslides and road conditions. In Odisha, some district administrations have announced closures following heavy rain and weather warnings.Odisha is among the states facing intense rainfall. The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rain in isolated areas, while warnings remain in force for several districts.Nabarangpur district administration has declared a holiday for all government-aided and private schools and Anganwadi centres on August 24 because of heavy to very heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and lightning warnings.Reports have also confirmed school closures in other affected Odisha districts, with Kalahandi among the areas facing flooding concerns following heavy rainfall.The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall in Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Sikkim, parts of the Northeast and southern India.Bihar is expected to receive isolated heavy rain from August 24, while Odisha remains under an extended period of heightened rainfall activity.Delhi-NCR is expected to see cloudy conditions and light rain at some places. No confirmed rain-related statewide school closure has been reported for Delhi.Similarly, no statewide closure has been confirmed for Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, West Bengal, Uttarakhand or Chhattisgarh based on the latest available updates.Parents and students should not treat an IMD weather warning as an automatic school holiday. Closure decisions are generally issued by the concerned district administration, education department or school authorities.Students should check their school's official website, mobile application, WhatsApp group or notice board. They should also monitor verified district administration announcements for last-minute changes, particularly in areas affected by flooding, waterlogging or landslides.Where a district administration has issued a closure order, students should follow that notification and avoid unnecessary travel during severe weather.
Article Summary: Odisha is among the states facing intense rainfall. The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rain in isolated areas. There is no nationwide school holiday for August 24. School closures are being decided locally according to rainfall, flooding, waterlogging, landslides and road conditions.

Article Title: Trump tariffs: What India can learn from Canada’s failed trade talks with US
Article Text:
Canada called off its trade negotiations with Trump administration on August 21, 2026. (AP file photo)

Why US-Canada trade negotiations were important

US offers little concessions

Why Canada called off the trade negotiations

What this means for India

Canada’s firm stance to call off trade negotiations with the US and the Donald Trump administration’s unpredictable policies hold key lessons for India, according to Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).Canada called off its trade negotiations with the US on August 21, 2026, and withdrew its negotiating team after realising that Washington was offering only limited tariff relief in exchange for concessions that could undermine Canadian manufacturing and constrain the country’s sovereignty.The US described the breakdown of three days of intensive trade negotiations with Canada as a “missed opportunity” after Ottawa suspended the talks and instructed its negotiating team to return home, while Washington imposed 50%t tariffs on Canadian goods.US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada had refused to conclude an agreement even though, according to him, the US had offered to provide Canada with the “best treatment of any major exporter” accessing the American market. Greer said Canada’s introduction of new demands and revisions to commitments made earlier in the talks had upset the balance that negotiators had reached.Ottawa said it would introduce “dollar-for-dollar” retaliatory tariffs from September 8.The move brought an end to talks that had started on February 1, 2025, after the first round of new US tariffs was imposed.The negotiations were notable because Canada and the US have enjoyed more than three decades of free trade. The arrangement began with the North American Free Trade Agreement, which took effect in 1994, and was later replaced by the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement in 2020. The USMCA continues to operate and allows most qualifying goods from North America to move between the countries without duties.The need for a new agreement arose after the Donald Trump administration introduced additional tariffs outside the USMCA framework, on top of the standard World Trade Organization, or most-favoured-nation, duties.Among the measures were Section 232 national-security tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian steel, aluminum, copper and related products, along with 25% duties on automobiles and parts. Washington also introduced separate tariffs covering lumber and wood products.The US additionally applied a 10% Section 301 tariff to a wide range of Canadian goods, arguing that Canada had not done enough to enforce its prohibition on imports linked to forced labour.It later used Section 338 to levy 50% duties on certain Canadian exports, including wine, cement, hockey equipment and other consumer products. Some of these tariffs were imposed even on goods that met USMCA rules of origin.The “WTO-violative” tariffs reduced the commercial certainty that the USMCA was intended to provide. Canada therefore entered the bilateral talks seeking exemptions, meaningful tariff cuts and safeguards against additional unilateral measures before the USMCA’s 2026 joint review.GTRI lists the limited and conditional relief that the US was willing to provide while continuing to introduce new demands.The US proposed cutting the 50% tariffs on steel and aluminum to 25%, but tied the reduction to restrictive quotas.The US offered to bring the tariff on vehicles manufactured in Canada down from 25% to 15%, but refused to provide the same treatment for medium- and heavy-duty trucks. This would have put Canadian-made Ford F-350, F-450 and F-550 trucks, along with General Motors’ Silverado, at a disadvantage.The US proposed temporary protection against broader Section 338 tariffs and suggested postponing 50% duties on roughly $20 billion worth of Canadian consumer and agricultural exports. However, the relief was reportedly tied to tight import quotas, concessions involving Canada’s supply-management system for dairy and other agricultural products, and the removal of provincial curbs on sales of American alcohol.The most contentious issue involved demands that went beyond traditional trade policy. The US wanted Canada to face limits on its ability to negotiate trade agreements independently, while also seeking preferential access to Canadian critical minerals.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney described the last-minute terms put forward by Washington as “uneconomic” and “unfair,” saying the US had demanded too much while offering too little in return.Ottawa determined that the proposed arrangement would keep significant US tariffs in place while also restricting Canada’s freedom to manage its trade relationships, strategic resources, agricultural system and cultural policies.Canada will now levy matching duties on selected US imports, including steel, dairy products, household appliances, agricultural machinery, pulp and paper, and electronics.Carney accepted that the retaliatory measures would push up prices at home and limit consumer choice. However, he argued that agreeing to an imbalanced deal would inflict greater long-term harm on Canadian industry and sovereignty.According to GTRI’s Ajay Srivastava, for India, which is negotiating its own trade agreement with the US, Canada’s experience offers a warning.“New Delhi should seek clear, binding and durable tariff concessions before making commitments on agriculture, digital regulation, critical minerals or government procurement,” he says.“An agreement that merely reduces some US tariffs while leaving Washington free to impose fresh duties under Sections 232, 301 or other domestic laws would offer little certainty,” he adds.India should therefore safeguard its regulatory and strategic autonomy and avoid making unilateral concessions outside the negotiating process. Any concessions should be made only when the gains are balanced, enforceable and protected from future unilateral tariff measures, he concludes.India and the US remain engaged in discussions for a trade deal. The Trump administration reduced the 50% tariffs imposed last year on India to 18% in February. However, the US Supreme Court later ruled that Trump’s reciprocal tariffs are illegal. The Trump administration has since then been looking for ways to impose tariffs on countries around the world.
Article Summary: Canada called off its trade negotiations with the US on August 21, 2026. It withdrew its negotiating team after realising that Washington was offering only limited tariff relief in exchange for concessions. The most contentious issue involved demands that went beyond traditional trade policy.
